name: Sliding Hot Dog & Sandwich Box
material: Printed paperboard tray and sleeve; liner and board specification confirmed for the filling
structure: Rectangular food tray sliding into a printed outer sleeve with cutout openings
intro: A tray-and-sleeve pack for a filled hot dog, roll or sandwich. The sliding construction differs from a stick sleeve or a hinged burger carton and needs clearance around the finished filling. Example artwork and food are not included.
measure: Filled roll length, width and maximum height, tray footprint and sleeve opening clearance
checks: Measure toppings and wrapping as well as the bread so the sleeve does not drag against the food.
Review how the tray slides and how the packed food is supported during handoff.
Confirm liner requirements and the intended holding conditions; the cutouts are not a tested ventilation claim.
question: How much clearance does a sliding hot dog box need?
answer: Measure the complete filled roll, including toppings and any liner. Check the tray depth and sleeve opening using a packed sample so the tray moves without scraping the filling. There is no universal clearance allowance for every menu item.
distinct: Sliding food tray with a separate sleeve, rather than the existing open corn-dog stick sleeve or hinged burger carton.

name: Mini Burger Sharing Box with Portion Insert
material: Printed board outer carton with a project-specific portion insert; contact layers confirmed for the menu
structure: Hinged sharing carton with a repeated grid of individual mini-burger positions
intro: Organize several mini burgers in one sharing carton rather than ordering a separate clamshell for every portion. The repeated burger-position insert is sized around your finished sliders, not around unrelated sauce cups or meal trays. Contents and artwork are presentation references.
measure: Finished slider diameter and height, portion count, spacing between portions and overall packed weight
checks: Confirm bun, topping and liner dimensions before choosing each insert position.
Review how staff load and remove portions without crushing neighboring burgers.
Check the lid clearance, carrying method and any separate sauce requirement using a complete sample.
question: Can one sharing box fit different slider sizes?
answer: The insert must be reviewed for the actual slider sizes and portion count. A layout that fits one bun diameter may not suit another. Send finished portion measurements and test a loaded sample before approving the grid and lid depth.
distinct: Repeated individual mini-burger insert in a sharing carton, distinct from single-burger clamshells and mixed meal trays with sauce positions.

name: Multi-Tray Catering Carrier Box
keyword: custom multi tray catering carrier boxes
material: Printed board outer carton; internal tray materials, support and liners confirmed separately
structure: Window-lid outer carrier arranged around multiple removable rectangular food trays
intro: Plan one outer carrier around several separate catering trays. This larger tray-based arrangement differs from a single meal presentation tray with small sauce positions. The pictured food containers illustrate fit; confirm the scope of tray supply separately from the outer carton.
measure: Each tray external length, width and height including rim and lid, tray count, outer footprint and total loaded mass
checks: Provide the exact food trays and lids; nominal capacity does not define the external rim size.
Agree the partition and support layout so individual trays can be lifted without shifting adjacent containers.
Test the loaded carrier and closure on the intended handoff route; no heat retention or carrying capacity is assumed.
question: Are the inner catering trays included?
answer: Confirm this in the quotation. The outer carton and inner food trays are separate specification items. Send the exact tray and lid dimensions and state whether you need carton-only supply or a coordinated pack; the reference image does not define the supplied contents.
distinct: Outer carrier for several removable full rectangular catering trays, not the existing individual mixed-portion meal presentation tray.

name: Meal & Drink Catering Box
keyword: custom meal and drink catering boxes
material: Printed paperboard outer and divider options; filled-load requirements confirmed by sample
structure: Closeable rectangular meal carton with a food area and separate drink-container positions
intro: Combine a meal and its drink containers inside one closeable catering carton. Unlike an open cup carrier or a raised serving tray, this brief needs to review drink height and separation within a closed outer pack. Cans, bottles and food shown are not included.
measure: Meal footprint, drink-container height and maximum diameter, divider positions and complete packed mass
checks: Use the actual can or bottle dimensions and review how it is separated from the food.
Check closed-lid clearance and the sequence for loading and removing the drink.
Describe condensation exposure and transit conditions before confirming the board and liner; do not assume spill containment.
question: Will the same carton fit cans and bottles?
answer: Not automatically. Bottle and can heights, diameters and closure shapes differ. Send both container specifications if you want a shared layout, then check the divider support, lid clearance and packed balance with samples.
distinct: Drink positions enclosed beside a meal in a closeable carton, distinct from open cup carriers and raised catering trays with cup slots.

name: Upright Sandwich Catering Box
material: Printed board outer with divider or support options; direct-contact liners reviewed separately
structure: Deep rectangular catering carton arranged for upright sandwich rows
intro: Present cut sandwiches upright in rows rather than laying them flat in a standard grazing tray. Size the carton and any row supports around the cut shape, filling and packed orientation. The pictured arrangement is a reference, not a fixed portion capacity or size offer.
measure: Cut sandwich base, filled thickness and upright height, row count and intended packing orientation
checks: Check that the sandwich stays upright without squeezing the filling.
Review row supports and liner placement with your actual bread and moist fillings.
Confirm the closed height and loading sequence on a sample; no chilled-storage or transit performance is assumed.
question: How many sandwiches fit in the catering box?
answer: Capacity depends on the cut shape, filled thickness, upright height and row layout. Send a portion sample or measurements and your target count. Confirm the usable internal dimensions with a loaded sample rather than using the reference image as a capacity promise.
distinct: Deep catering format organized around upright sandwich rows, rather than a shallow grazing compartment tray or graduated pyramid tray.

name: Four-Tray BBQ Packaging Carton
keyword: custom four tray BBQ packaging cartons
material: Printed board outer carton; tray materials, liners and support confirmed for the intended contents
structure: Closeable outer carton arranged around four separately lidded rectangular containers
intro: An outer packaging format arranged around four lidded containers for a BBQ-related order. Compare this closed-container layout with the existing open grill-component and meal-tray arrangements. This page covers the packaging brief, not a working grill, heating device or a guarantee that inner containers are included.
measure: External dimensions of all four containers including lids, complete packed weight and required outer footprint
checks: Specify the contents and exact lidded containers before approving the outer layout.
Confirm carton-only versus included tray or equipment supply in writing; no grill, fuel or cooking function is assumed.
Do not heat or burn the paperboard carton. Review filled-load handling and food-contact layers for the intended packaging use.
question: Is this a disposable grill or a box for lidded trays?
answer: This page specifies the outer packaging layout around four lidded containers. It does not establish that a grill, fuel, heater or inner containers are supplied. Identify the required components in the quotation, and never treat the paperboard carton as a cooking surface or burnable stove.
distinct: Four separately lidded container arrangement for an outer carton, distinguished from the existing open grill-component grid and open meal-tray layouts. Printed variants of this four-container arrangement are consolidated.
